candidates.attacker_control: An authenticated Karaf shell user controls the value of the `-o`/`--java-opts` option of `instance:start`/`instance:restart` and (through `instance:create`/`instance:clone`) the instance name and location that are also placed into the script (start.sh `cd ${dir}`). The webconsole instance plugin additionally passes the HTTP `javaOpts` parameter into the same start path, giving an HTTP/CSRF vector against admin sessions.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: I verified that javaOpts/instance names are never quoted, filtered or regex-validated in the instance module; that the command is not passed as a list but as one shell string; that `shell:exec` (the intended admin-only OS execution command) is restricted in etc/org.apache.karaf.command.acl.shell.cfg while no org.apache.karaf.command.acl.instance.cfg exists anywhere in the tree (searched); that SecuredSessionFactoryImpl.checkSecurity allows commands without ACL when no compulsory roles are set (system.properties documents this default); and that the JMX path to the same service is admin-guarded by jmx.acl.cfg (`* = admin`). I also checked that the shell command wrapping (SecuredCommand/SecuredSessionFactoryImpl) does enforce ACLs, so this is not a general ACL bypass but a missing/sanitization gap specific to the instance commands.
candidates.impact: Arbitrary OS command execution with the privileges of the Karaf process (typically the karaf service account), permitting privilege escalation from a viewer/manager shell user to full host code execution, persistence (e.g., storing malicious javaOpts in instance.properties so later starts re-execute it), and access to any file/credential the Karaf process can read. The injection is silent and requires no admin command.
candidates.prerequisites: Authenticated shell session (SSH/local console) or webconsole access; the `instance` feature installed (it is part of the standard/minimal feature sets); ability to create or reference an existing instance. No admin role is required for the shell path because the instance scope has no default ACL and no compulsory-role system property is set; on Linux/Unix the JPM path uses /bin/sh (Windows start.vbs resource is not present in this snapshot, so that path is unverified).
candidates.root_cause: InstanceServiceImpl builds a Java launch command by raw string concatenation, inserting the caller-supplied javaOpts (and, in the restart path, the instance name) without quoting or validation (lines 533-548 and 613-625). This string is passed to the JPM ProcessBuilder (lines 554-557 / 626-629), written into the generated script by ScriptUtils.filter (lines 103-113) and executed through /bin/sh (lines 42-45) as `nohup ${command} &` (start.sh line 28), so shell metacharacters in the option value are interpreted. The `instance` command scope also has no ACL configuration in any shipped distribution, and SecuredSessionFactoryImpl treats commands without a scope ACL as allowed when karaf.secured.command.compulsory.roles is unset (lines 225-239), so low-privileged shell users can reach the sink.
candidates.title: OS command injection in instance shell commands via unvalidated --java-opts / instance name
candidates.trace: instance:start -o <value> <name> (StartCommand.java lines 38-39, 54-75) -> InstanceImpl.start -> InstanceServiceImpl.startInstance (473-486) -> doStart (488-559): opts = javaOpts at 489-495, command = "java" + opts + ... at 533-548 -> ProcessBuilderFactoryImpl.newBuilder().command(command).start() (554-557) -> ProcessImpl.create (111-136) puts the full command into props for ScriptUtils.execute -> ScriptUtils copies unix/start.sh substituting ${command} (31-50, 103-113) and runs /bin/sh on it (44-45) -> start.sh line 28 executes `nohup ${command} &`, so shell metacharacters/substitutions in the option value execute as OS commands. The same interpolation exists in restartInstance (613-625, 626-629).
candidates.unverified: No code was executed or built and no PoC was run; the Windows execution path (start.vbs) is absent from the snapshot; operator deployments may add a restrictive instance ACL or compulsory roles that reduce reachability; it is unconfirmed whether this specific weakness is the case's intended ground truth.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-78 OS Command Injection (privilege escalation from authenticated shell user to OS code execution)

coverage_summary: Reviewed the assigned snapshot (1660 read-only main-source files; no tests, no history). Concentrated on: shell security and ACL enforcement (SecuredSessionFactoryImpl, SecuredCommand, CommandTracker, ACLConfigurationParser, GuardProxyCatalog, RegexCommandLoggingFilter), JAAS (Properties/Digest/LDAP/Publickey/JDBC/OsgiConfig modules, backing engines, keystore/encryption), management (KarafMBeanServerGuard, MBeanInvocationHandler, JMXSecurityMBeanImpl, ConnectorServerFactory, RmiRegistryFactory), webconsole authentication/plugins, SSH server and client commands, instance core/commands, util JPM process execution, KAR/profile/feature/config extraction and XML parsing (XmlUtils, JaxbUtil, Kar, FeatureConfigInstaller, ConfigRepositoryImpl), the HTTP proxy servlet, and shipped ACL/system-property defaults. Remaining modules (scheduler, subsystem, scr, obr, jms, jpa, audit, diagnostic, maven tooling, wrapper, docker, examples, archetypes, assemblies beyond ACL defaults) were inspected only by targeted searches, not file-by-file.
limitations: No execution, build, tests, scanners or runtime validation were performed; findings are source-evidence only.
Repository history/patches and external ground truth were not available (and were not to be consulted), so this could not be confirmed as the case's intended issue.
The snapshot has tests and binary-like resources removed, so Windows JPM scripts and test-visible behavior could not be inspected.
Not every one of the 1660 files was read line-by-line; several modules were covered only by targeted searches and spot checks.
Whether operators typically deploy an instance ACL or set karaf.secured.command.compulsory.roles affects real-world reachability of the candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: http/src/main/java/org/apache/karaf/http/core/internal/ProxyServlet.java lines 189-197 and 173-178: inverted Location header check (`if (locationHeader != null) throw ... but without location`) plus a cast of ServletException to IOException.
rejected_leads.reason: Looks anomalous, but both are error-path/functional defects (NIED NPE / ClassCastException) with only low-impact DoS on admin-configured proxies and no attacker-controlled privilege gain; not selected over the command injection.

rejected_leads.lead: instance/src/main/java/org/apache/karaf/instance/core/internal/InstanceServiceImpl.java lines 291-308: instance name/location used as a path (`loc = name`, `new File(storageLocation, loc)`) allowing creation of directories/files outside the instances directory.
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible path traversal in the same subsystem, but impact is file/directory creation (arbitrary write needs more setup) and it is a separate sink from the command-injection root cause; left unconfirmed rather than listed as a second candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: config/src/main/java/org/apache/karaf/config/core/impl/ConfigRepositoryImpl.java lines 153-166: `factoryPid + "-" + alias + ".cfg"` written under karaf.etc with attacker-controlled alias/factoryPid (config:edit --factory --alias; manager role).
rejected_leads.reason: Potential path traversal/arbitrary .cfg write but requires the manager role and writes properties-file content; lower severity and prerequisites than the instance injection.

rejected_leads.lead: features/core/src/main/java/org/apache/karaf/features/internal/service/FeatureConfigInstaller.java lines 100-134: feature config PID used to build `<pid>.cfg` paths under etc.
rejected_leads.reason: Reachable only via feature/config installation (admin-restricted by default ACLs) and impact is limited to config file placement; not pursued.
The KARAF-6090-style '..' filter is present and the Java File(parent, child) semantics neutralize absolute entry names in the paths I traced; no bypass found.

rejected_leads.lead: jaas/modules LDAP/Properties/JDBC login modules and jaas/config keystore code.
rejected_leads.reason: RFC2254 encoding is applied to the LDAP user name, the authentication=none downgrade is handled, SQL is parameterized, and password handling/digest logic showed no auth bypass in source review.
Allows SSH tunneling for any authenticated user, but this is an upstream design/config choice rather than a demonstrated injection or bypass.

rejected_leads.lead: Unrestricted shell built-ins (cat, source, env, etc.) for non-admin users in the default ACLs.
rejected_leads.reason: By-design shell behavior/config; the issue with concrete security impact is the OS command execution through the instance command sink.

summary: Apache Karaf 4.3.0-SNAPSHOT (main sources only, tests stripped, ~1660 files). I reviewed the security-relevant subsystems: shell command ACL/security (SecuredSessionFactoryImpl, SecuredCommand, ACLConfigurationParser, service guard), JAAS login/backing engines, JMX management guard and connector, webconsole authentication, SSH server/authenticator, instance management, JPM process execution, KAR/profile/feature extraction and config handling, JAXP/XML hardening, and the HTTP proxy servlet. The strongest source-supported issue is an OS command injection in the `instance` shell commands: caller-supplied `--java-opts` (and instance names) are concatenated into a command string that is substituted into a generated `/bin/sh` script and executed with `nohup ${command}`, with no quoting/validation. Because the distribution ships no `org.apache.karaf.command.acl.instance.cfg` and the shell default is "command without ACL = allowed", any authenticated shell user (e.g. viewer role) can reach this sink, unlike `shell:exec`, which is explicitly admin-only. No runtime confirmation was performed.
